references.text: "You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, so that you do not bear sin because of him." ([ref:3 Mos 19:17|Leviticus 19:17]) This Old Testament text gives the same command to rebuke one's brother or neighbor, which underlies Jesus' words about rebuking someone who sins.
Jesus gives in [ref:Matt 18:15|Matthew 18:15] a parallel teaching on going to a brother who has sinned and pointing it out – the same principle of admonishing a believing brother.

In [ref:Matt 18:21-22|Matthew 18:21-22], Peter asks how many times he should forgive his brother, and Jesus answers "seventy times seven." This expands on the instruction about forgiveness that follows repentance, as Luke 17:3 assumes.
The following verse [ref:Luk 17:4|Luke 17:4] expands the instruction by saying that one should forgive even seven times in a day if the brother turns back.
Paul instructs in [ref:Gal 6:1|Galatians 6:1] to restore someone caught in a transgression with gentleness – a practical outworking of the principle in Luke 17:3 about rebuking a brother who sins.
In [ref:Jak 5:19-20|James 5:19-20], believers are encouraged to bring back someone who has wandered from the truth. This reflects the same responsibility to rebuke and lead a brother to repentance.

"Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving each other, just as God in Christ forgave you" ([ref:Ef 4:32|Ephesians 4:32]). Paul emphasizes the duty of mutual forgiveness, which corresponds with Jesus' command to forgive those who turn back.
[ref:Kol 3:13|Colossians 3:13] instructs believers to bear with one another and forgive each other, just as the Lord has forgiven them – an echo of Jesus' teaching on forgiveness in Luke 17:3.

"A rebuke strikes deeper into a person of understanding than a hundred blows into a fool" ([ref:Ordsp 17:10|Proverbs 17:10]). This proverb highlights the value of rebuke, which Jesus commands toward a brother who sins.

In [ref:Matt 6:14-15|Matthew 6:14-15], Jesus says that if you forgive others, your heavenly Father will also forgive you – a fundamental condition for forgiveness linked to the instruction in Luke 17:3 to forgive those who repent.
